domains.name: Mobile Devices
domains.summary: Set up, configure and support laptops, phones and tablets.
topics: Laptop hardware: RAM, storage, batteries, keyboards, displays
Mobile accessories and connection methods (USB-C, Bluetooth, NFC, hotspot)
Mobile device network connectivity and app support
Display components: LCD, OLED, digitizer, inverter

domains.name: Networking
domains.summary: Networking fundamentals for supporting small offices and home networks.
topics: TCP and UDP ports and protocols
Networking hardware: switches, routers, APs, firewalls, PoE
Networked host services (DNS, DHCP, web, mail, syslog)
IP addressing: IPv4, IPv6, APIPA, static vs dynamic
SOHO network configuration and tools (crimpers, testers, toner)

domains.name: Hardware
domains.summary: Install, configure and maintain PC components and peripherals.
topics: Motherboards, CPUs, add-on cards and cooling
Printers and multifunction devices: laser, inkjet, thermal, impact

domains.name: Virtualization & Cloud
domains.summary: Virtualization and cloud computing concepts for IT support.
topics: Cloud models: public, private, hybrid, community
Cloud characteristics: elasticity, metered use, shared resources

domains.name: Hardware & Network Troubleshooting
domains.summary: Diagnose and fix hardware and network problems using a proven method.
topics: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power faults

domains.name: Operating Systems
domains.summary: Install, configure and manage Windows, macOS and Linux.
topics: Windows tools: Task Manager, MMC snap-ins, Control Panel, Settings
Command-line tools (ipconfig, sfc, chkdsk, robocopy, gpupdate)
macOS and Linux features and commands
OS installation, file systems and partitioning

domains.name: Security
domains.summary: Protect devices, users and data in a small business.
topics: Windows security settings: Defender, firewall, BitLocker, UAC

domains.name: Software Troubleshooting
domains.summary: Fix operating system, security and application problems.
topics: Common Windows OS problems and fixes

domains.name: Operational Procedures
domains.summary: Professional practices that keep IT support safe and reliable.

parts.summary: The hardware side: devices, networking, hardware, virtualization & cloud, and troubleshooting them.

questions.prompt: A user's smartphone battery drains quickly and the phone feels hot even when idle. What is the BEST first step?
choices: Check battery usage for a misbehaving app
questions.explanation: Start with the least invasive step: battery usage settings reveal apps running in the background and consuming power.

questions.prompt: Which technology lets a phone pay at a checkout terminal by holding it a few centimetres away?
questions.explanation: Near Field Communication (NFC) works over a few centimetres and is used for contactless payments.

questions.prompt: A laptop's display is very dim but an image is faintly visible with a flashlight. What has MOST likely failed?
questions.explanation: A faint image visible under a flashlight means the LCD panel works but the backlight (or inverter on older CCFL screens) does not.

questions.prompt: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TCP 443. HTTP is 80, SSH is 22 and RDP is 3389.

questions.prompt: A PC shows an IP address of 169.254.12.40. What does this indicate?
choices: It could not reach a DHCP server (APIPA)
It has a static public IP
questions.explanation: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA address, self-assigned when a DHCP server can't be reached.

questions.prompt: Which Wi-Fi standard is also known as Wi-Fi 6?
questions.explanation: 802.11ax is Wi-Fi 6 (and Wi-Fi 6E on 6 GHz). 802.11ac is Wi-Fi 5, 802.11n is Wi-Fi 4.

questions.prompt: Which protocol translates hostnames like example.com into IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS (port 53) resolves names to IP addresses.

questions.prompt: Which RAM type is used in most modern laptops due to its smaller size?
questions.explanation: SO-DIMM (small outline DIMM) modules are used in laptops and small form factor PCs.

questions.prompt: A technician needs the fastest storage option for a new desktop with an M.2 slot. What should they choose?
questions.explanation: NVMe SSDs use PCIe lanes and are far faster than SATA-based drives.

questions.prompt: Which RAID level provides mirroring with no striping?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives. RAID 0 stripes, RAID 5 stripes with parity, RAID 10 is a stripe of mirrors.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of thermal paste between a CPU and its heat sink?
choices: Fill microscopic gaps to improve heat transfer
questions.explanation: Thermal paste fills tiny air gaps so heat moves efficiently from the CPU to the heat sink.

questions.prompt: Which cloud model provides virtual machines while the customer manages the OS?
questions.explanation: With IaaS the provider supplies infrastructure; the customer manages the OS and everything above it.

questions.prompt: A Type 1 hypervisor is BEST described as:
choices: Software running on top of a host OS
A hypervisor running directly on hardware
questions.explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors like ESXi or Hyper-V Server run directly on hardware.

questions.prompt: A PC powers on, fans spin, but there is no display and it emits a repeating beep pattern. What should the tech do FIRST?
choices: Look up the POST beep code
questions.explanation: Beep codes are POST diagnostics; look them up for that BIOS vendor to identify the failing component.

questions.prompt: Users report a printer produces pages with a repeating smudge at the same interval. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Defects repeating at regular intervals point to a roller, drum or fuser with damage matching its circumference.

questions.prompt: A user can reach websites by IP address but not by name. What is the MOST likely issue?
questions.explanation: If IP access works but names fail, name resolution (DNS) is the problem.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command checks and repairs protected system files?
questions.explanation: System File Checker (sfc /scannow) scans and restores protected Windows system files.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool shows running processes and lets you end a frozen app?
questions.explanation: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) lists processes and can end unresponsive tasks.

questions.prompt: Which file system is used by default on modern macOS?
questions.explanation: APFS (Apple File System) is the default on modern macOS and iOS.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command changes file permissions?
questions.explanation: chmod changes permissions; chown changes ownership.

questions.prompt: An email appears to come from the CEO urgently asking an employee to buy gift cards. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Impersonating an executive by email to trick staff is phishing (business email compromise).

questions.prompt: Which is the MOST secure wireless encryption option?
questions.explanation: WPA3 is the current, strongest Wi-Fi security standard.

questions.prompt: Requiring a password and a code from an authenticator app is an example of:
questions.explanation: Something you know plus something you have is MFA.

questions.prompt: After a Windows update, a PC repeatedly crashes on startup. What should be tried FIRST?
choices: Boot into Safe Mode / use System Restore
questions.explanation: Safe Mode or System Restore can roll back the problematic change without data loss.

questions.prompt: Browser keeps redirecting to unknown search pages and shows pop-ups. What is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Redirects and pop-ups are classic signs of a browser hijacker or adware.

questions.prompt: What is the FIRST step in the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology?
questions.explanation: The process starts with identifying the problem, then establishing a theory of probable cause.

questions.prompt: Before opening a PC case, which should a technician use to prevent ESD damage?
questions.explanation: An antistatic wrist strap equalises charge between you and the equipment.

questions.prompt: Which document lists the hazards and safe handling of a chemical such as toner?
questions.explanation: A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) explains handling, hazards and disposal of materials.

questions.prompt: Which backup type copies only files changed since the last FULL backup and does not reset the archive bit?
questions.explanation: Differential backups grow until the next full backup; incrementals capture changes since the last backup of any kind.

questions.prompt: A user wants to share a phone's cellular data connection with a laptop over a USB cable. Which feature should be enabled?
questions.explanation: USB tethering shares the phone's mobile data with a computer through the cable. Wi-Fi calling routes voice calls over Wi-Fi and does not share data.

questions.prompt: A company wants to remotely wipe lost corporate phones and enforce passcode policies. Which solution should it deploy?
questions.explanation: MDM platforms enroll devices so administrators can push policies, enforce passcodes and wipe lost devices remotely.

questions.prompt: A laptop's touchpad works, but the cursor moves on its own while the user types. What should the technician check FIRST?
questions.explanation: Accidental palm contact is the usual cause; adjusting sensitivity or enabling palm rejection is quick and non-invasive.

questions.prompt: Which wireless technology is MOST commonly used to pair a smartwatch with a smartphone?
questions.explanation: Smartwatches use Bluetooth (often Bluetooth Low Energy) for a constant low-power link with the paired phone.

questions.prompt: A laptop user has to plug in a monitor, wired network, keyboard and charger every morning. Which accessory would let them connect all of these with one cable?
choices: A USB-C or Thunderbolt docking station
questions.explanation: A USB-C/Thunderbolt dock carries video, data, network and power delivery over a single connection to the laptop.

questions.prompt: A smartphone screen does not rotate when the device is turned sideways. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: Whether the screen digitizer is cracked
questions.explanation: Rotation lock is a simple software toggle and is the most common reason the display stays in one orientation.

questions.prompt: Which component in a laptop display converts the touch of a finger or stylus into input?
questions.explanation: The digitizer is the touch-sensitive layer that translates touches into coordinates; the inverter powers older CCFL backlights.

questions.prompt: A user's phone shows full Wi-Fi bars but email will not sync while connected to a hotel network. Websites in the browser redirect to a login page. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The phone's SIM card is faulty
The hotel's captive portal has not been accepted
questions.explanation: Captive portals block traffic until the user signs in or accepts terms, which is why browsing redirects to a login page.

questions.prompt: A technician is replacing a laptop's M.2 SSD. What should be done BEFORE removing the bottom panel?
choices: Disconnect the AC adapter and the internal battery
questions.explanation: Removing all power sources protects both the technician and components from shorts while working inside the laptop.

questions.prompt: Which hardware feature is required for a phone to use an eSIM profile instead of a physical SIM card?
choices: An embedded, reprogrammable SIM chip on the device
questions.explanation: An eSIM is a soldered, rewritable SIM chip that can download carrier profiles without a removable card.

questions.prompt: A user reports their phone's GPS location is inaccurate indoors but fine outside. What is the BEST explanation?
choices: Building materials block satellite signals, so the phone relies on less precise Wi-Fi and cell data
The phone needs a new SIM card
questions.explanation: GPS needs line of sight to satellites; indoors the device falls back to Wi-Fi and cell-tower positioning, which is less precise.

questions.prompt: A laptop's keyboard has several dead keys after a coffee spill. What is the MOST appropriate repair?
questions.explanation: Liquid damage to keyboard membranes is generally permanent, so the keyboard module should be replaced.

questions.prompt: A sales team needs their phones to sync corporate email, contacts and calendars from Microsoft Exchange. Which protocol is typically used?
questions.explanation: Exchange ActiveSync synchronizes mail, calendar and contacts between Exchange and mobile devices.

questions.prompt: A phone's battery is bulging and the screen is starting to lift from the frame. What should the technician do?
choices: Press the screen back down and seal it with adhesive
Fully charge the battery to recalibrate it
Put the phone in a freezer to shrink the battery
Stop using the device and replace the battery following safe-handling procedures
questions.explanation: A swollen lithium-ion battery is a fire risk; the device should be powered off and the battery replaced and recycled properly.

questions.prompt: A user wants to unlock their laptop with a fingerprint. Which component and Windows feature are needed?
choices: A smart card reader and BitLocker
A fingerprint reader and Windows Hello
questions.explanation: Windows Hello provides biometric sign-in using a compatible fingerprint reader or IR camera.

questions.prompt: Which port and protocol are used by Remote Desktop Protocol by default?
questions.explanation: RDP listens on TCP 3389 by default. Port 22 is SSH and 445 is SMB.

questions.prompt: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks and default gateways to clients?
questions.explanation: DHCP leases IP configuration to clients automatically; DNS only resolves names.

questions.prompt: Which port does SMB use for Windows file and printer sharing over TCP/IP?
questions.explanation: Modern SMB runs directly over TCP 445. Port 389 is LDAP and 143 is IMAP.

questions.prompt: A small office needs devices on the internet to reach an internal web server at 192.168.1.20. What should be configured on the router?
choices: A DMZ for every internal host
questions.explanation: Port forwarding maps an external port on the router's public IP to the internal server so outside clients can reach it.

questions.prompt: Which IPv4 address range is a private address space defined by RFC 1918?
questions.explanation: 172.16.0.0/12 is one of the three RFC 1918 private ranges; 169.254.0.0/16 is link-local and 224.0.0.0/4 is multicast.

questions.prompt: Which device forwards traffic based on MAC addresses within a single LAN?
questions.explanation: Switches operate at Layer 2 and use MAC address tables; routers forward between networks using IP addresses.

questions.prompt: Which cable type is required for a 10 Gbps Ethernet run of 100 meters over copper?
questions.explanation: Cat 6a supports 10GBASE-T to 100 m; Cat 6 only supports 10 Gbps to about 55 m.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to securely manage a network switch from the command line?
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts the remote session, while Telnet sends credentials in plaintext.

questions.prompt: Which wireless frequency band offers the greatest range but the most interference from devices like microwaves?
questions.explanation: 2.4 GHz penetrates walls best and travels farther, but it is crowded and shares spectrum with microwaves and Bluetooth.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to give a printer the same IP address every time while still managing it from the DHCP server. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: A reservation ties a MAC address to a specific IP so the device always receives the same lease.

questions.prompt: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: AAAA records hold IPv6 addresses; A records hold IPv4 addresses and MX records identify mail servers.

questions.prompt: Which DNS record is used by receiving mail servers to verify which servers are allowed to send email for a domain?
choices: TXT record containing an SPF policy
questions.explanation: SPF policies are published in TXT records and list the hosts authorized to send mail for the domain.

questions.prompt: Which network type connects devices across a city, such as several campus buildings linked by fiber?
questions.explanation: A metropolitan area network spans a city or large campus; a PAN covers only a few meters around a person.

questions.prompt: Which protocol and port are used to send outgoing email from a client to a mail server with encryption?
questions.explanation: Mail submission uses SMTP on 587 with STARTTLS; POP3 and IMAP are for retrieving mail.

questions.prompt: Which tool would a technician use to verify which pair is miswired at the end of a newly terminated Ethernet cable?
questions.explanation: A cable tester checks continuity and pinout for each pair, revealing opens, shorts and crossed pairs.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of a Power over Ethernet (PoE) injector?
choices: Add DC power to an Ethernet cable for a device such as an access point
Filter electrical noise from the network
questions.explanation: A PoE injector supplies power over the data cable when the switch itself does not provide PoE.

questions.prompt: Which protocol allows a network monitoring server to poll routers and switches for performance statistics?
questions.explanation: SNMP (UDP 161, traps on 162) is used to query and monitor network devices.

questions.prompt: Which IPv6 address is the loopback address?
questions.explanation: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback; fe80::/10 is link-local and ff02::1 is the all-nodes multicast group.

questions.prompt: A home user wants to extend Wi-Fi coverage to every room with multiple units that act as a single network with one SSID. Which solution fits BEST?
choices: A second router with a different SSID
questions.explanation: Mesh systems use several nodes that coordinate to provide one seamless SSID across the home.

questions.prompt: Which connector is commonly used to terminate coaxial cable for cable-modem internet service?
questions.explanation: Cable internet uses RG-6 coax terminated with F-type connectors; LC is a fiber connector.

questions.prompt: Which protocol uses UDP port 69 and is often used to transfer firmware images to network devices without authentication?
questions.explanation: TFTP is a simple, unauthenticated file-transfer protocol on UDP 69; SFTP runs over SSH on port 22.

questions.prompt: An office needs a device that inspects traffic and blocks connections based on rules about ports, protocols and applications. Which device should be installed?
questions.explanation: Firewalls filter traffic based on defined rules; switches and patch panels do not enforce security policy.

questions.prompt: Which RAID level stripes data with distributed parity and requires at least three drives?
questions.explanation: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across three or more disks and survives one drive failure; RAID 0 has no redundancy.

questions.prompt: Which RAID level combines mirroring and striping and needs a minimum of four drives?
questions.explanation: RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs, giving both performance and redundancy with at least four disks.

questions.prompt: A desktop power supply has a 24-pin connector. What does it connect to?
questions.explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector is the main motherboard power cable; CPUs use separate 4/8-pin EPS connectors.

questions.prompt: A user needs to connect a modern graphics card that requires a 16-pin power connector. Which connector standard is this?
questions.explanation: High-end GPUs use the 16-pin 12VHPWR (revised as 12V-2x6) connector, which can deliver up to 600 W.

questions.prompt: Which expansion slot is used by most modern discrete graphics cards?
questions.explanation: Current GPUs use PCIe x16 slots for maximum bandwidth; AGP and PCI are legacy.

questions.prompt: A server administrator wants memory that can detect and correct single-bit errors. Which type should be purchased?
questions.explanation: Error-correcting code memory detects and fixes single-bit errors, which is important for servers.

questions.prompt: A motherboard has four DIMM slots color-coded in pairs. Why should two identical modules be installed in matching-color slots?
questions.explanation: Installing matched modules in the paired slots lets the memory controller run in dual-channel mode for more bandwidth.

questions.prompt: Which storage interface is used by an M.2 SSD that reaches speeds above 3,000 MB/s?
questions.explanation: NVMe drives use PCIe lanes and greatly exceed SATA III's practical ~550 MB/s limit.

questions.prompt: Which hard drive characteristic MOST affects the performance of a mechanical drive?
choices: Number of SATA ports on the motherboard
questions.explanation: Higher RPM (e.g., 7,200 vs 5,400) reduces rotational latency and improves throughput on HDDs.

questions.prompt: A technician must build a workstation for 3D rendering. Which component upgrade will MOST improve rendering in GPU-accelerated software?
choices: A high-end discrete graphics card with more VRAM
questions.explanation: GPU-accelerated renderers depend on GPU cores and VRAM, so a stronger graphics card gives the biggest gain.

questions.prompt: Which firmware security feature verifies that boot loaders are signed by trusted keys before the OS loads?
questions.explanation: Secure Boot in UEFI checks digital signatures on boot components to block rootkits and unsigned loaders.

questions.prompt: Windows 11 requires a hardware chip that stores encryption keys and supports BitLocker. What is it?
questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0, a secure cryptoprocessor that stores keys and measurements used by BitLocker and Secure Boot.

questions.prompt: A PC's clock resets to a default date every time it is unplugged. Which component should be replaced?
questions.explanation: The CMOS (CR2032) battery keeps the real-time clock and firmware settings powered when the system is unplugged.

questions.prompt: Which printer type uses heated elements to darken special coated paper, as often seen in receipt printers?
questions.explanation: Direct thermal printers apply heat to heat-sensitive paper; no ink or toner is used.

questions.prompt: In a laser printer, which step uses heat and pressure to bond toner to paper?
questions.explanation: The fuser assembly melts toner onto the paper with heated rollers; exposing is when the laser writes the image to the drum.

questions.prompt: A law office needs to print multi-part carbonless forms. Which printer type is required?
questions.explanation: Only impact printers physically strike the page, transferring the image through every layer of multi-part forms.

questions.prompt: A technician is replacing the printhead in an inkjet printer and wants to prevent streaky output. What should be done after installation?
choices: Run the printhead alignment and cleaning utility
questions.explanation: Inkjet printers need head alignment and cleaning after maintenance; fusers and corona wires are laser components.

questions.prompt: Which 3D printer component deposits melted filament layer by layer?
questions.explanation: In FDM printers, the hot end melts filament and the nozzle lays it down in layers on the build plate.

questions.prompt: Which display panel type offers the best color accuracy and viewing angles among common LCD types?
questions.explanation: IPS panels are known for accurate color and wide viewing angles; TN panels are faster but have poor angles.

questions.prompt: A designer wants a monitor with true blacks because each pixel produces its own light. Which display technology should they choose?
questions.explanation: OLED pixels are self-emissive and can turn off completely, giving true blacks without a backlight.

questions.prompt: Which connector carries both video and USB data and can also deliver power to a laptop?
questions.explanation: USB-C can carry DisplayPort video, USB data and USB Power Delivery on a single cable.

questions.prompt: A user wants a backup storage device that several home computers can access over the network. Which device should be recommended?
questions.explanation: A network-attached storage device shares files over the LAN to multiple clients.

questions.prompt: A desktop with a 450 W power supply randomly shuts down under gaming load after a GPU upgrade. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The power supply cannot provide enough wattage for the new GPU
questions.explanation: A higher-draw GPU can exceed the PSU's capacity, causing shutdowns under load; a higher-rated PSU is needed.

questions.prompt: Which type of storage device has no moving parts and uses NAND flash?
questions.explanation: Solid-state drives store data in NAND flash with no spinning platters or heads.

questions.prompt: Which cooling solution circulates liquid through a pump and radiator to remove CPU heat?
questions.explanation: AIO liquid coolers pump coolant from a CPU block to a radiator where fans dissipate the heat.

questions.prompt: Which BIOS/UEFI setting must be enabled for a hypervisor to run 64-bit virtual machines efficiently on an Intel CPU?
questions.explanation: Hardware virtualization extensions (VT-x on Intel, AMD-V on AMD) are needed by hypervisors and are often disabled by default.

questions.prompt: A company uses a web-based email and office suite that the provider fully manages. Which cloud service model is this?
questions.explanation: Software as a Service delivers complete applications; the customer only manages users and data.

questions.prompt: Developers want to deploy code without managing servers or operating systems, while the provider supplies the runtime. Which model fits?
questions.explanation: Platform as a Service provides the runtime and middleware so developers just deploy their applications.

questions.prompt: A business keeps sensitive workloads in its own data center but bursts to a public cloud during busy seasons. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines private infrastructure with public cloud resources that work together.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic allows resources to scale up and down automatically to match demand?
questions.explanation: Elasticity lets cloud resources grow or shrink automatically as workload changes.

questions.prompt: Several hospitals share a cloud built to meet the same healthcare compliance requirements. Which deployment model is this?
choices: Private cloud for a single tenant
questions.explanation: A community cloud is shared by organizations with common requirements such as regulatory compliance.

questions.prompt: Which type of hypervisor runs as an application on top of an existing desktop OS?
questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors such as VirtualBox or VMware Workstation run on a host operating system.

questions.prompt: A technician wants to test malware behavior safely and then revert the system to a clean state. Which VM feature helps MOST?
questions.explanation: Snapshots capture the VM's state so it can be rolled back after testing.

questions.prompt: Which technology packages an application with its dependencies and shares the host OS kernel instead of running a full guest OS?
questions.explanation: Containers such as Docker isolate applications while sharing the host kernel, making them lighter than VMs.

questions.prompt: Employees log in from any device to a full Windows desktop that runs in the company's data center. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Virtual desktop infrastructure hosts desktops centrally and streams them to client devices.

questions.prompt: A VM needs to communicate with the host only, without reaching the physical network. Which virtual network mode should be used?
questions.explanation: Host-only networking creates a private network between the host and its VMs with no outside access.

questions.prompt: A VM must appear on the physical LAN with its own IP address from the office DHCP server. Which network mode should be configured?
questions.explanation: Bridged mode connects the VM's virtual NIC directly to the physical network as a peer device.

questions.prompt: Which cloud feature bills customers only for the compute time and storage they actually consume?
questions.explanation: Metered (measured) service tracks usage so customers pay for what they consume.

questions.prompt: A PC makes a loud clicking noise and Windows reports disk read errors. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Back up the user's data immediately
questions.explanation: Clicking indicates a failing mechanical drive; preserving data comes before any repair or replacement.

questions.prompt: A computer shows a 'bootable device not found' error after a new drive was installed. What should be checked FIRST?
questions.explanation: Adding a drive can change boot priority; confirming the boot order points to the OS drive is the quickest fix.

questions.prompt: A desktop powers on for a second and then shuts off with no POST. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A short or failing power supply
questions.explanation: Instant power-off before POST often points to PSU failure or a short such as a misplaced standoff.

questions.prompt: A laptop shuts down without warning after 20 minutes of heavy use, and the fan sounds loud. What should the technician check?
questions.explanation: Overheating from clogged vents or a failing fan causes thermal shutdowns under load.

questions.prompt: A new RAM module was installed and the PC now beeps continuously and does not display anything. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Reseat the RAM and verify compatibility
questions.explanation: Beep codes after a memory upgrade typically mean the module is not seated or is incompatible.

questions.prompt: Laser printer output smears and toner rubs off with a finger. Which component is MOST likely faulty?
questions.explanation: If toner is not fused to the paper it wipes off, which indicates a failing fuser assembly.

questions.prompt: A laser printer frequently pulls several sheets at once. Which part should be cleaned or replaced?
questions.explanation: The separation pad ensures only one sheet feeds at a time; a worn pad causes multiple-sheet feeds.

questions.prompt: An inkjet printer prints pages with missing horizontal lines in the text. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Run the nozzle check and head-cleaning utility
questions.explanation: Missing lines usually mean clogged nozzles, which the built-in cleaning cycle can clear.

questions.prompt: Laser printer pages come out completely blank. What is a common cause?
choices: The toner cartridge's sealing tape was not removed
questions.explanation: A new cartridge with its seal still in place cannot deliver toner, producing blank pages.

questions.prompt: Users report that an entire floor lost network access at the same time. What is the MOST likely point of failure?
questions.explanation: A simultaneous outage for many users points to shared infrastructure, such as the floor's switch.

questions.prompt: A user's PC has intermittent network drops. The technician notices the cable runs across the floor next to a large motor. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Unshielded twisted pair near motors or power equipment can pick up EMI, causing errors and drops.

questions.prompt: A wireless laptop connects to Wi-Fi but speeds are very slow in a crowded apartment building. What is the BEST step?
choices: Use a Wi-Fi analyzer and move to a less congested channel or 5 GHz
questions.explanation: Channel congestion from neighboring networks degrades throughput; changing channel or band helps.

questions.prompt: A user cannot connect to the network and the NIC link lights are off. What should be checked FIRST?
questions.explanation: No link lights means no physical layer connection; check the cable and port before anything else.

questions.prompt: Two PCs on the network show a 'duplicate IP address' warning. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A static IP that overlaps the DHCP scope
questions.explanation: Manually assigned addresses inside the DHCP range can conflict with leased addresses.

questions.prompt: A monitor displays an image with a strong color tint and missing colors. What should the technician check FIRST?
choices: The video cable and its connectors for bent pins or looseness
questions.explanation: Missing colors often come from a damaged or loose video cable, especially VGA with bent pins.

questions.prompt: A projector image shuts off after a few minutes and the overheat light is on. What should be done?
choices: Clean the air filter and vents
questions.explanation: Clogged projector filters block airflow and trigger thermal shutdown to protect the lamp.

questions.prompt: An LCD monitor has a single pixel that is always lit red. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A stuck pixel remains on in one color; a dead pixel stays black.

questions.prompt: A RAID 5 array reports one failed disk but the volume is still accessible. What should the technician do?
choices: Replace the failed drive and let the array rebuild
Run chkdsk /f on every disk individually
questions.explanation: RAID 5 tolerates one failure; replacing the bad drive and rebuilding restores redundancy.

questions.prompt: A PC fails to POST and the technician smells burning plastic near the motherboard. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Power off and unplug the system immediately
questions.explanation: A burning smell indicates a failing component; removing power prevents further damage or fire.

questions.prompt: A user's laptop battery will only hold a charge for 15 minutes and is several years old. What is the BEST solution?
questions.explanation: Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity with age and charge cycles; replacement restores runtime.

questions.prompt: A desktop's system clock drifts and BIOS settings revert to defaults after power loss. What should the technician replace?
questions.explanation: A depleted CMOS battery can no longer preserve firmware settings and the clock.

questions.prompt: A user has a slow internet connection only on their desktop, which shows a link speed of 100 Mbps on a gigabit network. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A damaged cable or one with a broken pair
questions.explanation: Gigabit Ethernet needs all four pairs; a damaged pair causes the link to fall back to 100 Mbps.

questions.prompt: A technician suspects a wall jack is not connected to the correct switch port. Which tool should be used to trace the cable?
questions.explanation: A tone generator and probe identify which cable at the patch panel belongs to the wall jack.

questions.prompt: After a GPU driver update, a PC displays visual artifacts and colored blocks in games. What should be tried FIRST?
questions.explanation: If artifacts appear immediately after a driver change, rolling back the driver is the least invasive test.

questions.prompt: A computer is running slowly and SMART reports a high count of reallocated sectors. What does this indicate?
choices: The drive needs to be defragmented
The drive is failing and should be replaced soon
questions.explanation: Rising reallocated sector counts are a key SMART warning of imminent drive failure.

questions.prompt: A Windows PC shows a blue screen referencing a specific driver file after a new webcam was installed. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Boot to Safe Mode and remove or roll back the webcam driver
questions.explanation: A BSOD that names a newly added driver points to that driver; Safe Mode allows its removal.

questions.prompt: An application crashes every time it starts after a recent update. Which Windows tool shows the error details?
questions.explanation: Event Viewer's Application log records crash events, faulting modules and error codes.

questions.prompt: A user's PC takes several minutes to reach a usable desktop after login. What should the technician check FIRST?
questions.explanation: Many startup programs slow logon; disabling unneeded ones in Task Manager's Startup tab is a quick fix.

questions.prompt: A user receives a certificate warning on every HTTPS site. Other users on the same network are fine. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The website certificates have all expired
The PC's system date and time are incorrect
questions.explanation: An incorrect system clock makes valid certificates appear expired or not yet valid.

questions.prompt: A user's files have been renamed with a strange extension and a note demands payment. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Disconnect the PC from the network
questions.explanation: Isolating the infected system prevents ransomware from spreading to network shares and other hosts.

questions.prompt: In the CompTIA malware removal process, a technician has remediated the system, scheduled scans and run updates. What is the NEXT step?
choices: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
questions.explanation: After scans and updates, System Restore is re-enabled and a clean restore point created; educating the user is the final step.

questions.prompt: During malware removal, why should System Restore be disabled in Windows?
choices: To free disk space for scans
To prevent infected restore points from reintroducing the malware
questions.explanation: Restore points may contain infected files; disabling it removes them so the malware cannot return.

questions.prompt: A phone app closes immediately every time it is opened. What should be tried FIRST?
choices: Force stop the app and clear its cache
questions.explanation: Clearing the cache or force-stopping resolves many app crashes without data loss.

questions.prompt: A user's phone has unusually high data usage and new apps appeared that the user did not install. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Unknown apps and unexplained data use are common signs of a compromised mobile device.

questions.prompt: A Windows PC cannot boot and displays 'BOOTMGR is missing'. Which tool should be used to repair it?
choices: Windows Recovery Environment with bootrec commands
questions.explanation: WinRE's Startup Repair or bootrec /rebuildbcd can repair a damaged boot configuration.

questions.prompt: A user's Windows profile loads with a temporary profile and their desktop files are missing. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Windows loads a temporary profile when it cannot read the user's profile, often due to corruption.

questions.prompt: Documents will not print and the print queue shows jobs stuck. What should the technician do FIRST?
questions.explanation: Restarting the spooler clears stuck jobs and often restores printing.

questions.prompt: A user reports that their browser shows a security warning for a well-known bank site, and the address bar shows a slightly misspelled domain. What is happening?
choices: The user has reached a spoofed site, likely through phishing or typosquatting
The PC needs a new NIC
questions.explanation: Misspelled domains mimicking real sites are typosquatting or phishing pages designed to steal credentials.

questions.prompt: A PC is very slow and Task Manager shows 100% disk usage from a single unknown process. What should the technician do?
choices: Research the process and scan the system for malware
questions.explanation: An unknown process consuming resources may be malicious; identifying it and scanning is the right approach.

questions.prompt: After installing a new application, Windows becomes unstable. The user did not create a backup. What is the BEST quick recovery option?
choices: Use System Restore to return to a restore point from before the install
questions.explanation: System Restore reverts system files and settings to an earlier point without affecting personal files.

questions.prompt: A user's Windows PC shows 'Your PC ran into a problem' repeatedly during boot. Which option should be tried before reinstalling the OS?
choices: Startup Repair from the Windows Recovery Environment
questions.explanation: Startup Repair automatically fixes many boot problems and is less disruptive than a reinstall.

questions.prompt: An application displays 'missing DLL' errors when launched. What is the BEST fix?
questions.explanation: A repair or reinstall restores the application's required DLL files.

questions.prompt: A user's phone will not connect to corporate email after a password change. What should be done?
choices: Update the saved password in the phone's mail account
questions.explanation: The device keeps trying the old password; updating it in the account settings resolves the issue.

questions.prompt: A browser runs slowly and displays unwanted toolbars. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Remove unwanted extensions and reset browser settings
questions.explanation: Malicious or unnecessary extensions are a frequent cause of slow, cluttered browsers.

questions.prompt: Windows Update fails repeatedly with the same error code. What is a good next step?
questions.explanation: The troubleshooter resets update components and fixes many common update failures.

questions.prompt: A user reports their phone screen does not respond to touch after an OS update, though it worked before. What should be tried FIRST?
questions.explanation: A soft reboot resolves many post-update glitches and is the least invasive step.

questions.prompt: A desktop app runs very slowly and Resource Monitor shows memory usage near 100%. What is the BEST long-term fix?
choices: Add more RAM or close unneeded programs
questions.explanation: Memory exhaustion forces heavy paging; more RAM or fewer running programs improves performance.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command displays the IP address, subnet mask and default gateway of all adapters?
questions.explanation: ipconfig /all shows full adapter configuration, including DNS servers and MAC addresses.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command shows the path packets take to a destination, hop by hop?
questions.explanation: tracert lists each router hop and its latency on the way to the destination.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command queries DNS servers to troubleshoot name resolution?
questions.explanation: nslookup sends DNS queries and shows which server answered and what records were returned.

questions.prompt: Which command forces an immediate refresh of Group Policy on a Windows client?
questions.explanation: gpupdate /force reapplies all policy settings; gpresult only reports which policies applied.

questions.prompt: Which command shows which Group Policy objects were applied to the current user and computer?
questions.explanation: gpresult /r summarizes the resultant set of policy for the user and computer.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command-line tool can create, delete and format partitions?
questions.explanation: diskpart manages disks, partitions and volumes from the command line.

questions.prompt: Which command scans a volume for file system errors and bad sectors?
questions.explanation: chkdsk /r locates bad sectors and recovers readable information; sfc checks system files instead.

questions.prompt: Which command repairs the Windows component store when sfc cannot fix corrupted files?
questions.explanation: DISM repairs the component store that sfc relies on to replace damaged system files.

questions.prompt: Which command maps a network share to drive letter Z: in Windows?
questions.explanation: net use connects a drive letter to a UNC path on a file server.

questions.prompt: Which robust Windows command copies large directory trees and can resume interrupted transfers?
questions.explanation: robocopy (Robust File Copy) supports mirroring, retries and restartable mode for large copies.

questions.prompt: Which Windows edition is required to join a computer to an Active Directory domain?
questions.explanation: Home editions cannot join domains; Pro, Enterprise and Education can.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature, unavailable in Home editions, encrypts entire drives?
questions.explanation: BitLocker full-volume encryption is included with Pro, Enterprise and Education editions.

questions.prompt: Which Control Panel or Settings tool lets a user change which app opens .pdf files?
questions.explanation: Default apps settings associate file types and protocols with specific applications.

questions.prompt: Which Windows utility shows real-time CPU, memory, disk and network usage per process, including which files a process is using?
questions.explanation: Resource Monitor provides detailed per-process resource usage, including open file handles and network connections.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool lets a technician configure services to start automatically, manually or be disabled?
questions.explanation: The Services console sets startup type and lets you start, stop or restart services.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Management Console snap-in is used to create local users and groups on Windows Pro?
questions.explanation: Local Users and Groups (lusrmgr.msc) manages local accounts and group memberships.

questions.prompt: Which tool runs a program automatically at a set time each day in Windows?
questions.explanation: Task Scheduler triggers programs or scripts based on time or events.

questions.prompt: Which Windows file system supports file permissions, encryption and large volumes?
questions.explanation: NTFS supports ACL permissions, EFS encryption, compression and very large volumes.

questions.prompt: A user needs a USB drive to work with both Windows and macOS and store files larger than 4 GB. Which file system should be used?
questions.explanation: exFAT is supported by both platforms and has no 4 GB file size limit like FAT32.

questions.prompt: Which is the default file system for most modern Linux distributions?
questions.explanation: ext4 is the standard journaling file system for many Linux distributions.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command runs a single command with administrative privileges?
questions.explanation: sudo executes one command as root (or another user) according to sudoers policy.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command changes the owner of a file?
questions.explanation: chown changes file ownership; chmod changes permissions.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command searches inside files for lines matching a pattern?
questions.explanation: grep searches file contents for text patterns; find locates files by name or attributes.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command displays running processes and their resource usage in real time?
questions.explanation: top continuously updates a list of processes with CPU and memory usage.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command shows how much free space each mounted file system has?
questions.explanation: df -h reports disk free space in human-readable units; free shows memory.

questions.prompt: Which package manager command installs software on Debian- and Ubuntu-based systems?
questions.explanation: apt is the package manager for Debian-based distributions.

questions.prompt: Which macOS feature provides automatic, incremental backups to an external drive?
questions.explanation: Time Machine performs hourly incremental backups to an external or network disk.

questions.prompt: Which macOS utility securely stores passwords, certificates and Wi-Fi keys?
questions.explanation: Keychain stores credentials and certificates encrypted for the user.

questions.prompt: On a Mac, which tool can be used to repair disk errors with the First Aid feature?
questions.explanation: Disk Utility's First Aid checks and repairs file system errors on macOS volumes.

questions.prompt: Which macOS feature quickly searches for files, apps and settings?
questions.explanation: Spotlight indexes the system and provides fast search with Command+Space.

questions.prompt: A company plans a deployment where Windows is installed from the network on many PCs at once. Which boot method should be enabled on the PCs?
questions.explanation: Preboot Execution Environment lets PCs boot from the network to receive an OS image.

questions.prompt: A user wants to keep their files and apps while upgrading from Windows 10 to Windows 11. Which installation type should be used?
questions.explanation: An in-place upgrade preserves user data, settings and applications.

questions.prompt: An attacker follows an employee through a secure door without badging in. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Tailgating (piggybacking) is gaining physical access by following an authorized person.

questions.prompt: Someone watches a user type their PIN at an ATM. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: Shoulder surfing is observing someone's screen or keypad to capture sensitive information.

questions.prompt: A user receives a text message with a link claiming their package is delayed and requesting payment details. What is this?
questions.explanation: Smishing is phishing via SMS text messages.

questions.prompt: A caller pretends to be from the help desk and asks a user for their password. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: Vishing is voice phishing, using phone calls to trick users into revealing information.

questions.prompt: An attacker sets up a wireless access point with the same SSID as a coffee shop's network to capture traffic. What is this called?
questions.explanation: An evil twin impersonates a legitimate SSID to lure users and intercept their traffic.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware disguises itself as a legitimate program to trick users into installing it?
questions.explanation: A Trojan appears useful but carries a malicious payload; worms spread on their own.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware spreads automatically across networks without user interaction?
questions.explanation: Worms self-replicate by exploiting vulnerabilities, spreading without user action.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware hides deep in the OS or firmware to conceal its presence from security tools?
questions.explanation: Rootkits gain privileged access and hide processes and files from detection.

questions.prompt: Which principle states users should have only the access they need to perform their jobs?
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits accounts to the minimum permissions necessary.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature prompts users for approval before a program makes system-level changes?
questions.explanation: UAC asks for consent or admin credentials before elevated actions run.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature warns users before running unrecognized downloaded apps and blocks known malicious sites?
questions.explanation: SmartScreen checks reputation of downloads and websites to block known threats.

questions.prompt: Which wireless authentication method uses a RADIUS server to authenticate each user with individual credentials?
questions.explanation: Enterprise mode uses 802.1X and RADIUS for per-user authentication rather than a shared key.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used by authentication servers to centralize AAA for network access, such as Wi-Fi and VPN?
questions.explanation: RADIUS provides centralized authentication, authorization and accounting for network access.

questions.prompt: A user's account becomes locked after five incorrect password attempts. Which security control is this?
questions.explanation: Lockout policies stop brute-force attacks by locking an account after repeated failed attempts.

questions.prompt: Which type of attack tries every possible password combination until one works?
questions.explanation: Brute-force attacks systematically try all combinations; dictionary attacks use word lists.

questions.prompt: An attacker inserts malicious SQL statements into a website's login form. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: SQL injection manipulates database queries through unsanitized input fields.

questions.prompt: Which attack intercepts communication between two parties so the attacker can read or alter traffic?
questions.explanation: In an on-path attack the attacker sits between victims, eavesdropping on or modifying traffic.

questions.prompt: A vulnerability is being actively exploited before the vendor has released a patch. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A zero-day is a flaw exploited before a fix is available.

questions.prompt: Which method makes data on a hard drive unrecoverable before disposal by physically destroying it?
questions.explanation: Physical destruction guarantees data cannot be recovered; formatting leaves recoverable data.

questions.prompt: Which method erases a magnetic hard drive by exposing it to a strong magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Degaussing scrambles magnetic domains, rendering HDD data unreadable; it does not work on SSDs.

questions.prompt: A company wants staff to badge in and also have their palm scanned before entering the server room. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Combining something you have (badge) with something you are (biometrics) is multifactor authentication.

questions.prompt: Which physical security control uses two sets of doors so only one person can pass at a time?
questions.explanation: An access control vestibule traps a person between two doors to prevent tailgating.

questions.prompt: Which feature allows users to log in once and access multiple applications without re-entering credentials?
questions.explanation: SSO authenticates the user once and grants access to multiple connected services.

questions.prompt: Which Windows NTFS permission is required for a user to modify a file's contents but not change its permissions?
questions.explanation: Modify allows reading, writing and deleting; Full control additionally allows changing permissions and ownership.

questions.prompt: A file with Read share permission and Full control NTFS permission is accessed over the network. What is the effective permission?
questions.explanation: When share and NTFS permissions combine over the network, the most restrictive permission applies.

questions.prompt: Which home router setting should be changed FIRST when setting up a new device?
questions.explanation: Default credentials are publicly known; changing them prevents unauthorized administration.

questions.prompt: A security policy requires that data on lost laptops cannot be read. Which control BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest even if the drive is removed from a lost device.

questions.prompt: Which feature in Windows Defender Firewall allows a specific application to communicate through the firewall?
choices: A port-forwarding rule on the PC
questions.explanation: Allow rules (exceptions) permit traffic for specific programs or ports while keeping the firewall enabled.

questions.prompt: After implementing a fix, what is the NEXT step in the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology?
choices: Establish a theory of probable cause
Document findings and close the ticket
Verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures
questions.explanation: After implementing the solution, verify full functionality and add preventive measures; documentation comes last.

questions.prompt: In the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology, what should a technician do if a theory is NOT confirmed?
choices: Establish a new theory or escalate
questions.explanation: If testing does not confirm the theory, the technician forms a new theory or escalates.

questions.prompt: Which document describes the planned change, its risk, rollback plan and approval before a major system update?
questions.explanation: A change request documents purpose, scope, risk analysis and backout plan for change-board approval.

questions.prompt: In change management, what is the purpose of a backout plan?
choices: To list users affected by the change
To restore the original state if the change fails
To assign the change to a technician
questions.explanation: A backout (rollback) plan defines how to undo the change if problems occur.

questions.prompt: Which backup strategy keeps three copies of data on two different media with one copy offsite?
questions.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule protects data from local disasters and single-media failures.

questions.prompt: A nightly job backs up only what changed since the previous night's job, whether that job was full or partial. Which backup type is this?
questions.explanation: Incremental backups capture changes since the last backup, making them fast but requiring every increment to restore.

questions.prompt: Which device protects a server from short power outages and allows a graceful shutdown?
questions.explanation: An uninterruptible power supply provides battery power during outages so systems can shut down safely.

questions.prompt: What is the proper way to dispose of old lithium-ion laptop batteries?
choices: Recycle them according to local regulations
Store them indefinitely in a desk drawer
questions.explanation: Batteries contain hazardous materials and must be recycled per environmental regulations.

questions.prompt: When lifting a heavy server, what is the correct technique?
choices: Lift with the legs while keeping the back straight
Bend at the waist and lift quickly
Lift with arms extended away from the body
questions.explanation: Proper lifting uses the legs, keeps the load close and the back straight to avoid injury.

questions.prompt: A technician finds illegal content on a user's PC during a repair. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Stop work, preserve the evidence and report it per company policy
Copy the files to a USB drive for later review
Ignore it and finish the repair
questions.explanation: Incident response requires preserving evidence and following the chain of custody by reporting through proper channels.

questions.prompt: Which document tracks who has handled evidence from collection to court?
questions.explanation: Chain of custody records each person who handled evidence, protecting its integrity.

questions.prompt: Which agreement defines guaranteed response and resolution times between a provider and customer?
questions.explanation: A service-level agreement specifies performance commitments such as uptime and response times.

questions.prompt: Which policy outlines what employees may and may not do with company computers and networks?
questions.explanation: An AUP defines permitted use of organizational IT resources.

questions.prompt: A customer is upset about a delayed repair. What should the technician do?
choices: Tell the customer they are wrong
Listen actively, avoid arguing and explain the next steps
Hang up and call back later
questions.explanation: Professional communication means listening, staying calm and setting clear expectations.

questions.prompt: A technician is working at a customer's desk and their personal phone rings. What should they do?
choices: Let it go to voicemail unless it is an emergency
Ask the customer to wait while they take the call
questions.explanation: Avoiding personal interruptions shows respect for the customer's time.

questions.prompt: Which type of data includes names, Social Security numbers and home addresses and must be protected?
questions.explanation: Personally identifiable information can identify individuals and is protected by privacy laws.

questions.prompt: Which scripting file extension is used for Windows PowerShell scripts?
questions.explanation: PowerShell scripts use the .ps1 extension; .sh is a Linux shell script and .bat is a batch file.

questions.prompt: Which remote access tool lets a help desk technician view and control a user's Windows session with the user's permission?
questions.explanation: Quick Assist and Remote Assistance let a technician share control of the user's screen after the user grants permission.
